data.text/markdown: In this tutorial, we illustrate the network optimization example in the Section 4.2 of the paper: Exact Verification of First-Order Methods via Mixed-Integer Linear Programming. Suppose that we are given a set of ||(n_s||) supply nodes and ||(n_d||) demand nodes, which constructs a bipartite graph with capacitated directed edges from supply nodes to demand nodes. Let ||(A_s||) and ||(A_d||) be submatrices corresponding to supply nodes and demand nodes, respectively. For each edge ||(i||), let ||(c_i||) be the flow capacity, ||(\mu_i||) be the cost of sending a unit of flow, and ||(f_i||) be the variable representing the amount of flow sent. Finally, let ||(b_s \ge 0||) be the vector of supply amounts available at each supply node and ||(x \le 0||) be the vector of requested demand amount for each demand node. Consider the following minimum cost network flow problem: ||[\begin{array}{ll} \text{minimize} & \mu^T f \\ \text{subject to} & A_s f \le b_s \\ & A_d f = x \\ & 0 \le f \le c. \end{array}||]

We solve this problem using the standard Chambolle-Pock method, or Primal-dual Hybrid Gradient (PDHG): ||[\begin{array}{rcl} z^{k+1} &=& \Pi_{[0, c]} \big( z^k - \eta (\mu + A_s^T v^k - A_d^T w^k) \big) \\ v^{k+1} &=& \max \big\{ v^k + \eta \big( - b_s + A_s (2 z^{k+1} - z^k) \big) \big\} \\ w^{k+1} &=& w^k + \eta \big( x - A_d (2 z^{k+1} - z^k) \big). \end{array}||]We choose ||(\eta = 0.5 / \| \begin{bmatrix} - A_s^T & A_d^T \end{bmatrix} \|_2||).
We first simulate the PDHG algorithm on given problem instances by randomly sampling the parameter ||(x||) (demand vector) over the parameter set ||(\mathcal{X}||).
